svg.text: Skygraph — what sits between the agent and the repository
The agent never walks the folder. It asks the graph, gets exactly what it needs, and spends its context on the work instead of on rediscovery.
Claude Code · Codex · any MCP host
Brings the model and does the work. Holds no index and reads no folder to build context.
14 read-only tools, over MCP · stdio locally, HTTP when hosted
The tool surface — shaped so the agent needs fewer round trips
FIND — before you know the name
find_symbols
list_repos · list_files
map_coverage
UNDERSTAND — look before you fetch
describe_symbol · expand_symbol
outline_file
read_source ← the only one that
returns code text
TRAVERSE — what a grep cannot do
related_symbols
file_imports

TRUST — how good is this index?
repo_summary
index_health
an agent that cannot see the gaps
will answer over them
skygraph — the index, and how it is built
one SQLite file · yours · never leaves the machine
Five ontologies
What may exist in the graph. Declared,
so nothing undeclared is ever written.
code_ontology files, symbols, calls
data_ontology entities, fields, keys
api_ontology endpoints, operations
deploy_ontology images, config, pipelines
link the joins between them
link is the one a text search cannot fake
Three extraction tiers
A file is read by the best tier that
claims it, and drops if it cannot cope.
1 · native a real AST parse
2 · query declarative patterns
3 · model optional, needs a key
Every row records the tier that produced
it. A parsed fact and a model's guess are
never mixed without saying which.
Built once, refreshed by delta
Every file carries a content hash. A second run
reads only what changed, replaces just those rows,
and prunes what was deleted.
This is the whole economic argument. Re-indexing a
repository after a day's work costs the few files you
touched, not the repository.
indexed 3 · unchanged 1,847 · removed 1
read-only · the repository is never written to
The project folder the person chose
Source, schemas and migrations, API specs and route handlers, Dockerfiles and pipelines.
Whatever a tier can read becomes graph. Whatever it cannot is recorded as a gap, with the reason,
and `index_health` shows it — because a quiet gap is answered over rather than around.
Your model key — optional
Only tier 3 uses it, only for files the
first two tiers could not read, and only
if you supply one. With no key skygraph
still works; it just knows less, and says so.
